job_title: Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager – Power Generation (Gas Turbines)
description:
Jereh Energy Equipment and Technologies is expanding its power generation supply chain capabilities and is looking for a Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager with hands-on experience sourcing
**gas turbine equipment, components, and services**
.

This position will lead supplier and category strategy supporting gas turbine power generation systems, rotating equipment, generators, controls, and associated mechanical and electrical systems. We are looking for someone who knows the turbine supply base, understands the commercial side of sourcing, and can work directly with engineering, operations, quality, project teams, and suppliers.

**Key Responsibilities**

• Lead strategic sourcing and category management for gas turbine equipment, components, repair services, and MRO requirements

• Develop sourcing strategies for industrial and aero-derivative gas turbine applications

• Source mechanical and electrical categories including rotating equipment, generators, control systems, valves, piping, fabrication, castings, forgings, machining, and related components

• Identify, qualify, develop, and manage domestic and international suppliers

• Lead commercial negotiations and long-term agreements, including MSA, SEA, and LTA structures

• Manage supplier performance across cost, quality, delivery, capacity, and risk

• Drive cost reduction, cost avoidance, supplier development, and localization opportunities

• Support CAPEX, OPEX, project procurement, aftermarket, and MRO sourcing requirements

• Partner with engineering, operations, quality, finance, and project management on supplier and sourcing decisions

• Monitor supplier KPIs, market conditions, lead times, capacity, commodity trends, and supply risk

• Support supplier recovery and expedited requirements when project or field schedules are at risk

**Required Qualifications**

• 7+ years of strategic sourcing, procurement, category management, or supply chain experience

• Direct sourcing experience supporting
**gas turbines, power generation, rotating equipment, or closely related energy equipment**

• Experience sourcing turbine components, engineered equipment, fabrication, machining, electrical equipment, controls, valves, piping, or MRO services

• Demonstrated supplier negotiation and contract management experience

• Experience with long-term supplier agreements, supplier development, cost reduction, and performance management

• Experience working with engineering, operations, quality, and project teams

• ERP/MRP experience such as SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards, or comparable systems

• Ability to travel domestically and internationally based on business requirements

**Preferred Background**

• Experience with OEMs or supply chains associated with
**GE Vernova / GE Power, Baker Hughes, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Solar Turbines**
, or comparable turbine organizations

• Experience with industrial or aero-derivative gas turbine platforms

• Existing knowledge of the U.S. and global turbine supplier market

• Experience supporting power generation projects, turbine services, aftermarket operations, gas compression, LNG, or oil and gas applications

• APICS, CPSM, CPIM, CSCP, Six Sigma, or related supply chain certification

Reworld partners with businesses by offering cutting-edge engineering and innovative solutions, to help customers reduce, reuse, recycle and recover value from waste streams and meet or exceed their sustainability goals.

**About The Role**
The Senior Global Commodity Manager – Chemicals Reagents will lead enterprise-wide commodity strategy, sourcing, supplier partnership management, and cost optimization for chemicals and reagents used across waste-to-energy plants, waste-processing facilities, and other industrial operations.
  
  
The role will manage a significant portfolio that includes lime, ammonia, urea, water and wastewater-treatment chemicals, carbon products, industrial gases, solidification materials, lubricants, and other chemicals and reagents required by the business.
  
  
A key focus of this position is building strong partnerships with strategic suppliers to improve total cost, product quality, technical support, service, innovation, and supply reliability. This is a senior individual-contributor position that leads cross-functional teams and may provide category-management guidance or mentorship to other procurement professionals.

* Develop and execute enterprise-wide commodity strategies for chemicals and reagents.
* Lead the complete sourcing process, including market analysis, RFI/RFP/RFQ development, supplier evaluation, negotiation strategy, contracting, implementation, and benefit tracking.
* Build and manage strategic relationships with key chemical and reagent suppliers.
* Lead supplier business reviews, performance scorecards, escalations, and joint improvement plans.
* Hold suppliers accountable for cost, safety, quality, service, delivery, technical support, innovation, and supply continuity.
* Partner with suppliers, Operations, and Logistics to optimize freight, delivery methods, inventory levels, tank utilization, and supply reliability.
* Identify opportunities for supplier consolidation, product standardization, demand management, alternative products, and total-cost improvement.
* Balance enterprise commodity strategies with site-specific technical and operational requirements.
* Partner with facility leadership, regional procurement, Operations, Engineering, Environmental, Safety, Finance, Legal, and Logistics.
* Support supplier and chemical-product qualification, including specification reviews, technical evaluations, plant trials, risk assessments, and stakeholder approvals.
* Monitor chemical markets, feedstock costs, freight, production capacity, and supply-chain risks.
* Develop backup suppliers, alternative products, and business-continuity plans for critical chemicals.
* Analyze spend, pricing, consumption, supplier performance, and market data and provide recommendations to leadership.
* Deliver measurable savings, cost avoidance, risk reduction, working-capital improvement, and service improvement.
* Support other procurement priorities based on business needs.
* Up to 30% travel time, could be international travel

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement, Business, or a related field.
* At least 7 years of experience in strategic sourcing, commodity management, procurement, supply chain, or commercial management.
* Candidates must have either:

+ Procurement or commodity-management experience within the chemical industry; or
+ A chemistry, chemical-engineering, or related technical background combined with significant procurement or strategic-sourcing experience.

* Experience developing and executing category or commodity strategies.
* Demonstrated success managing strategic suppliers and improving supplier performance.
* Experience leading competitive sourcing events and negotiating complex supply agreements.
* Ability to understand chemical applications, specifications, cost drivers, logistics, storage, handling requirements, and supply risks.
* Strong analytical, negotiation, communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills.

description:
Who we are
  
  
For more than 40 years, Reworld has been a leader in sustainable waste solutions, providing our customers with innovative solutions that help them achieve carbon-negative outcomes.
  
  
Our Vision
  
  
Reworld is leading the charge to a carbon-negative future through revolutionary sustainable materials management solutions that reduce, reuse, recycle and reimagine waste for the benefit of society and the environment.
  
  
Our Business
  
  
Reworld partners with businesses by offering cutting-edge engineering and innovative solutions, to help customers reduce, reuse, recycle and recover value from waste streams and meet or exceed their sustainability goals.
  
  
Our Value
  
  
Reworld's differentiator comes from our ecosystem of technology, facilities and partnerships, trusted by the world’s largest organizations to reimagine waste management for a smarter, more sustainable world.
  
  
All that we’re missing is you. Apply today!
  
  
**About The Role**
The Senior Global Commodity Manager – Chemicals Reagents will lead enterprise-wide commodity strategy, sourcing, supplier partnership management, and cost optimization for chemicals and reagents used across waste-to-energy plants, waste-processing facilities, and other industrial operations.
  
  
The role will manage a significant portfolio that includes lime, ammonia, urea, water and wastewater-treatment chemicals, carbon products, industrial gases, solidification materials, lubricants, and other chemicals and reagents required by the business.
  
  
A key focus of this position is building strong partnerships with strategic suppliers to improve total cost, product quality, technical support, service, innovation, and supply reliability. The role will lead complex cross-functional sourcing initiatives and balance enterprise strategies with the technical and operating requirements of individual facilities.
  
  
This is a senior individual-contributor position that leads cross-functional teams and may provide category-management guidance or mentorship to other procurement professionals.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute enterprise-wide commodity strategies for chemicals and reagents.
* Lead the complete sourcing process, including market analysis, RFI/RFP/RFQ development, supplier evaluation, negotiation strategy, contracting, implementation, and benefit tracking.
* Build and manage strategic relationships with key chemical and reagent suppliers.
* Lead supplier business reviews, performance scorecards, escalations, and joint improvement plans.
* Hold suppliers accountable for cost, safety, quality, service, delivery, technical support, innovation, and supply continuity.
* Partner with suppliers, Operations, and Logistics to optimize freight, delivery methods, inventory levels, tank utilization, and supply reliability.
* Identify opportunities for supplier consolidation, product standardization, demand management, alternative products, and total-cost improvement.
* Balance enterprise commodity strategies with site-specific technical and operational requirements.
* Partner with facility leadership, regional procurement, Operations, Engineering, Environmental, Safety, Finance, Legal, and Logistics.
* Support supplier and chemical-product qualification, including specification reviews, technical evaluations, plant trials, risk assessments, and stakeholder approvals.
* Monitor chemical markets, feedstock costs, freight, production capacity, and supply-chain risks.
* Develop backup suppliers, alternative products, and business-continuity plans for critical chemicals.
* Analyze spend, pricing, consumption, supplier performance, and market data and provide recommendations to leadership.
* Deliver measurable savings, cost avoidance, risk reduction, working-capital improvement, and service improvement.
* Support other procurement priorities based on business needs.
* Up to 30% travel time, could be international travel

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement, Business, or a related field.
* At least 7 years of experience in strategic sourcing, commodity management, procurement, supply chain, or commercial management.
* Candidates must have either:

+ Procurement or commodity-management experience within the chemical industry; or
+ A chemistry, chemical-engineering, or related technical background combined with significant procurement or strategic-sourcing experience.

* Experience developing and executing category or commodity strategies.
* Demonstrated success managing strategic suppliers and improving supplier performance.
* Experience leading competitive sourcing events and negotiating complex supply agreements.
* Ability to understand chemical applications, specifications, cost drivers, logistics, storage, handling requirements, and supply risks.
* Strong analytical, negotiation, communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. The Senior Global Sourcing Manager, Radar is the domain expert for the radar commodities for Anduril Industries. This is a proactive, high-impact role in securing critical components, materials, and services that power our products. This role will be responsible for developing new supplier and new sourcing partnerships that can be incorporated into new products, as well as existing products to improve their technologies, cost, and quality. There is broad internal cross functional partnership to evaluate supplier opportunities, while ensuring commercial agreements, intellectual property, and statement of works are accurate and well established prior to pipelining.

job_title: Sr. Global Sourcing Manager, AWS Infrastructure Services
description:
**Description**
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
  
  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides a highly reliable, scalable, and low-cost cloud platform that powers thousands of businesses in over 190 countries. AWS Infrastructure Service (AIS) organization works to deliver cutting-edge solutions to source, build and maintain our socially responsible data center supply chains. We are a team of highly-motivated, engaged, and responsive professionals who enable the core sustainable infrastructure of AWS. Come join our team and be a part of history as we deliver results for the largest cloud services company on Earth!
  
  
The AIS Power & Cooling team is looking for a results-oriented individual to own sourcing and supply management for Data Center Power & Cooling Equipment. Our Procurement Managers are experts in their industries who deliver the supply that helps drive the explosive growth of AWS.
  
  
As a member of the Power and Cooling Procurement Team, you will manage the end-to-end global sourcing and supply chain for one or more of the categories that reside within the Power and Cooling Equipment space supporting AWS Data Center build projects. This role's primary responsibility is to maintain unconstrained supply on a global scale for the responsible categories and work with our internal customers and business partners to understand demand signals and drive the appropriate supply strategies to deliver continuity of supply. This has to be achieved while enabling procurement with low cost structure and flexibility in adapting to volatile demand.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Develop, implement, and manages sourcing and supply chain strategies on a global scale for mission critical complex electrical equipment
* Drive the category strategies to maximize capacity availability and optimize total cost of ownership
* Support new product introduction program for mission critical complex electrical equipment to ensure seamless design transition and enable inception-to-scale
* Develop and maintain supplier capacity modeling
* Understand demand inputs and position supply to support unconstrained growth at AWS scale in both the short-term and long-term horizons
* drive leading supply chain practices and initiatives
* Partner with engineering teams to drive NPI initiatives and value-engineering initiatives.
* Drive innovation through the supply chain and influence industry practices
* Develop analytical reports to deliver information to business partners and stakeholders that support improved decision making
* Manage supplier lead times and drive them to meet AWS business requirements

job_title: Senior Global Commodity Manager - Chemicals, Reagents, Fuel
description:
Who we are
  
  
For more than 40 years, Reworld has been a leader in sustainable waste solutions, providing our customers with innovative solutions that help them achieve carbon-negative outcomes.
  
  
Our Vision
  
  
Reworld is leading the charge to a carbon-negative future through revolutionary sustainable materials management solutions that reduce, reuse, recycle and reimagine waste for the benefit of society and the environment.
  
  
Our Business
  
  
Reworld partners with businesses by offering cutting-edge engineering and innovative solutions, to help customers reduce, reuse, recycle and recover value from waste streams and meet or exceed their sustainability goals.
  
  
Our Value
  
  
Reworld's differentiator comes from our ecosystem of technology, facilities and partnerships, trusted by the world’s largest organizations to reimagine waste management for a smarter, more sustainable world.
  
  
All that we’re missing is you. Apply today!
  
  
**About The Role**
The Senior Global Commodity Manager – Chemicals Reagents will lead enterprise-wide commodity strategy, sourcing, supplier partnership management, and cost optimization for chemicals and reagents used across waste-to-energy plants, waste-processing facilities, and other industrial operations.
  
  
The role will manage a significant portfolio that includes lime, ammonia, urea, water and wastewater-treatment chemicals, carbon products, industrial gases, solidification materials, lubricants, and other chemicals and reagents required by the business.
  
  
A key focus of this position is building strong partnerships with strategic suppliers to improve total cost, product quality, technical support, service, innovation, and supply reliability. The role will lead complex cross-functional sourcing initiatives and balance enterprise strategies with the technical and operating requirements of individual facilities.
  
  
This is a senior individual-contributor position that leads cross-functional teams and may provide category-management guidance or mentorship to other procurement professionals.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute enterprise-wide commodity strategies for chemicals and reagents.
* Lead the complete sourcing process, including market analysis, RFI/RFP/RFQ development, supplier evaluation, negotiation strategy, contracting, implementation, and benefit tracking.
* Build and manage strategic relationships with key chemical and reagent suppliers.
* Lead supplier business reviews, performance scorecards, escalations, and joint improvement plans.
* Hold suppliers accountable for cost, safety, quality, service, delivery, technical support, innovation, and supply continuity.
* Partner with suppliers, Operations, and Logistics to optimize freight, delivery methods, inventory levels, tank utilization, and supply reliability.
* Identify opportunities for supplier consolidation, product standardization, demand management, alternative products, and total-cost improvement.
* Balance enterprise commodity strategies with site-specific technical and operational requirements.
* Partner with facility leadership, regional procurement, Operations, Engineering, Environmental, Safety, Finance, Legal, and Logistics.
* Support supplier and chemical-product qualification, including specification reviews, technical evaluations, plant trials, risk assessments, and stakeholder approvals.
* Monitor chemical markets, feedstock costs, freight, production capacity, and supply-chain risks.
* Develop backup suppliers, alternative products, and business-continuity plans for critical chemicals.
* Analyze spend, pricing, consumption, supplier performance, and market data and provide recommendations to leadership.
* Deliver measurable savings, cost avoidance, risk reduction, working-capital improvement, and service improvement.
* Support other procurement priorities based on business needs.
* Up to 30% travel time, could be international travel

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement, Business, or a related field.
* At least 7 years of experience in strategic sourcing, commodity management, procurement, supply chain, or commercial management.
* Candidates must have either:

+ Procurement or commodity-management experience within the chemical industry; or
+ A chemistry, chemical-engineering, or related technical background combined with significant procurement or strategic-sourcing experience.

* Experience developing and executing category or commodity strategies.
* Demonstrated success managing strategic suppliers and improving supplier performance.
* Experience leading competitive sourcing events and negotiating complex supply agreements.
* Ability to understand chemical applications, specifications, cost drivers, logistics, storage, handling requirements, and supply risks.
* Strong analytical, negotiation, communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills.
* Demons

job_title: Sr Procurement Manager - Data Center Modularization, Data Center Sourcing and Procurement
description:
**Description**
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
  
  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a dynamic, growing business unit within Amazon.com that provides a broad set of infrastructure services including computing power, storage options, networking and databases available on demand. We are the leader in cloud computing and our pioneers are embracing innovation, building the future, and making history! The Infrastructure team provides AWS and Amazon.com with the compute, network and data center capacity that are the foundations of the retail and cloud business.
  
  
Amazon is seeking a motivated and data-driven category manager to support the Americas data center build out. The candidate should have strong supply chain and procurement skills, analytical and financial acumen , communication capabilities and a hands-on passion to dive-deep into Data Center design and modularization opportunities. Additionally, candidate must have proven skills in managing large-scale supply chain and procurement improvement projects.
  
  
As a Category Manager, you will create and implement sourcing strategies for at least one construction category - Data Center Modularizatiom and collaborate with internal business partners and suppliers to drive efficiencies, reduce risks, and costs for Amazon. You will develop mechanisms and metrics to hold suppliers accountable for performance and delivery. You will drive results through methods that include competitive bidding, negotiating, and analyzing data and market trends for your category.
  
  
The ideal candidate thinks long term, drives multiple initiatives, communicates appropriately and influences customers and suppliers at all levels. You will be collaborative, but also work with significant autonomy. Lightedge is evolving its Procurement function to support the organization’s continued growth and scale. We are building a team of strategic procurement category managers and subject matter experts with expertise across the data center lifecycle, including facilities development and build-outs, capital equipment, ongoing facilities support, and technology.
  
  
The team will partner with business leaders to strengthen sourcing strategies, supplier relationships, commercial agreements, and purchasing practices that support both expansion and daily operations

Reporting to the Director of Global Direct Procurement, this individual will own the global semiconductor spend and serve as the primary procurement leader for one of the company's most critical commodities.

* Develop and execute global semiconductor commodity strategies that balance business growth objectives, cost competitiveness, supply continuity, and risk mitigation.

Revolutionize infrastructure procurement by driving strategic sourcing and innovative solutions that power global cloud computing infrastructure! Join our dynamic team and play a critical role in shaping the future of technology procurement across complex construction supply chains.
  
  
You will be instrumental in developing advanced procurement strategies that optimize our data center construction ecosystem. By leveraging your analytical skills and strategic thinking, you'll create transformative approaches that reduce costs, mitigate risks, and enhance supplier performance across our expansive infrastructure network.
  
  
We are a collaborative and forward-thinking group dedicated to building the technological infrastructure that powers global cloud computing. Our team values creativity, continuous learning, and a passion for solving complex challenges that shape the future of technology.

* Collaborate with internal stakeholders to align procurement strategies with business objectives

Your day will be filled with dynamic challenges that blend strategic planning, collaborative problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making. You'll engage with cross-functional teams, analyze market trends, and develop innovative sourcing strategies that drive operational excellence. Each day you will interact with different teams responsible for all aspects of the data centers. You will have the opportunity to work on projects locally and globally.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
  
  
**About AWS**
Diverse Experiences
  
  
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
  
  
Why AWS?
  
  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
  
  
Inclusive Team Culture
  
  
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.
  
  
Mentorship & Career Growth
  
  
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
  
  
Work/Life Balance
  
  
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

* Supplier Relationship Management: Develop and nurture robust relationships with key chemical suppliers, fostering strategic partnerships that enhance security of supply, sustainability, and continuous improvement across North American sites.
* Risk & Contract Management: Proactively identify supply chain risks across the chemical network, developing and implementing preventive and mitigating controls to ensure uninterrupted manufacturing operations and strict regulatory compliance
* Financial & Data Analytics: Perform rigorous spend analyses and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) assessments tailored to the chemical portfolio. Build frameworks for Working Capital (TWC) improvements—focusing on payment terms and inventory optimization—while applying sound accounting principles and financial reporting standards.

A day in the life
  
  
As a Procurement Manager on the Data Center Construction Procurement team, you will own the end-to-end commercial relationship with General Contractors (GCs) delivering AWS data centers. **Day To Day You Will**
Drive competitive sourcing events — develop RFP strategies, evaluate contractor qualifications, and lead award recommendations for some of the largest construction programs in the industry.
  
  
Negotiate and manage contracts — structure contract amendments, negotiate change orders, and hold GCs accountable to cost, schedule, and safety commitments.
  
  
Partner cross-functionally — work alongside Construction, Design, Legal, Finance, and Program Management to remove blockers, align on delivery milestones, and ensure data center capacity comes online on time.
  
  
Analyze cost and risk — benchmark GC pricing, identify cost-savings opportunities, and flag commercial risks before they become schedule impacts.
  
  
Influence at scale — develop procurement playbooks, contract standards, and lessons-learned that raise the bar across AWS's global data center portfolio.
  
  
You will support projects across multiple regions and have the opportunity to shape how AWS procures and delivers data center construction — locally and globally.

**About Fluidstack**
We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.
  
  
We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.
  
  
**We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!**
How We Operate
  
  

* Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.
* Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.
* Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.
* Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.
* Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

**The Supply Chain Team**
**Examples of key problems the team is working on**

* Supply tens of gigawatts of compute, the largest build out of compute in history. Qualify and dual-source across every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline.
* Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build redefines speed in this industry, and it lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint.
* Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had, and turn that foresight into a structural edge.

* Own the data center mechanical category: CDUs, chillers, pumps, dry coolers, and piping packages for liquid-cooled builds.
* Negotiate supply agreements with mechanical OEMs covering price, lead time, and factory capacity across a multi-year pipeline.
* Dual-source CDU and chiller platforms and drive the qualification work that makes the second source usable.
* Coordinate with manufacturing and design so equipment specs freeze early enough to buy at the lead times the market gives.

**What We're Looking For**

* The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.
* You've sourced major mechanical equipment (chillers, CDUs, AHUs, pumps) for data center or industrial programs.
* You've negotiated with mechanical OEMs on multi-year committed volumes.
* You know liquid cooling equipment well enough to challenge a spec or a price with substance.
* You've managed factory schedules and witness points so delivery dates held.
* Bonus: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Modular skid packages. Factory acceptance testing. Refrigerant and coolant markets.

Lumafield was founded in 2019 to upgrade manufacturing.

**Description**
Amazon is seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join the Global Corporate Procurement (GCP) Team. This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of a team that has a meaningful and measurable impact on Amazon’s success. At Amazon, our vision is to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Our passion for invention leads us to pioneer and globalize new businesses and customer offerings daily. As we rapidly become the world’s largest consumer of services in many categories, the Corporate Procurement team is fueling our explosive growth by identifying innovative sourcing strategies and negotiating sustainable, long-term partnerships. We are seeking a skilled Strategic Sourcing Manager with experience leading complex sourcing initiatives across Employee Services.
  
  
Key leadership traits required include the ability to influence and form partnerships with business leaders, and operational excellence in managing multiple complex and competing priorities simultaneously. Strategic Sourcing Managers are expert practitioners in the tools for creating competitive environments and have a bias for decision-making rooted in data and analytics. They routinely influence vendor relationships by advising Amazon leaders across multiple stakeholder groups on the direction of sourcing projects in support of business goals. If you are looking for a new challenge in a fast-paced, innovative company, come make history with Amazon’s Global Corporate Procurement department.
  
  
At Amazon, we believe that in-person collaboration is essential to our culture and innovation. While we allow flexibility for personal circumstances, we generally expect employees to work from our offices five days a week. This approach has consistently shown that spontaneous interactions, rapid problem-solving, and the energy of in-person teamwork led to better results for our customers. Our data shows that teams working together in person are more effective at making complex decisions, onboarding new team members, and fostering the kind of creative collaboration that has driven Amazon's success. The serendipitous hallway conversations and impromptu whiteboarding sessions that happen naturally in an office environment have proven invaluable to our invention process and maintaining our high bar for excellence.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Establishing strong relationships with internal business stakeholders; building a strong understanding of strategic business direction, requirements and priorities across assigned suppliers and/or spend categories
* Dive deep across multiple business units to leverage our supplier base with the goal of optimizing performance, quality, and cost
* Evaluate supplier core competencies and competitive positioning using industry cost models and benchmarking; leveraging key-insights to inform and support the strategic sourcing strategy development process
* Managing the fundamentals of sourcing and supplier engagement activities including RFx, spend pattern analysis, contract analysis, bid evaluation, negotiations, and supplier consolidation
* Identifying sourcing opportunities by leveraging spend analysis tools and engage with stakeholders to consolidate requirements over categories, suppliers and geographies
* Work with business and finance leaders to identify and drive savings and controllership improvements, optimizing the return on investment and total cost of ownership
* Providing guidance to internal stakeholders on procurement processes and best-practice tools, such as category management, supplier evaluation and supplier diversity

A day in the life
  
  
Your morning might start with a cross-functional alignment call for an upcoming RFP involving three business units, followed by analyzing bid responses and building a recommendation deck for senior leadership. After lunch, you're on a negotiation call with a strategic supplier's C-suite to finalize contract terms, then pivoting to a spend review with Finance to validate savings actuals against targets. You'll close the day by coaching a business partner through the supplier evaluation framework for an upcoming engagement. No two days look the same — you'll balance long-range strategic planning with hands-on execution, often managing five or more active sourcing engagements simultaneously across different stages of the lifecycle.
  
  
**About The Team**
Global Corporate Procurement (GCP) manages Amazon's indirect spend across Employee Services, Marketing, Professional Services, Technology, Logistics, and Real Estate & Facilities. We're a global team of sourcing professionals who combine analytical rigor with creative problem-solving to deliver sustainable value at scale. Our culture values deep ownership, intellectual curiosity, and a bias for action — we move fast, but we move smart. You'll be joining a team where your work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to Amazon's bottom line.

This position serves as the central point of contact for assigned areas of responsibility and is responsible for processing and validating requests for supplies made by assigned departments or for specific product lines. Cincinnati, OH, United States

**Education**

* Minimum Required: High School Diploma or GED.
* Preferred: Bachelor's degree in Business, Purchasing Management, Supply Chain Management, or a related field.

**Certification**

* No certification required.

**Experience**

* Minimum Required: 1 to 2 years of relevant purchasing, procurement, materials management, or related experience.
* Preferred: 3 to 5 years of healthcare purchasing, supply chain, or materials management experience.

**Responsibilities**
**Purchasing Materials and Supplies**

* Receive and review purchase requisitions for completeness, contract compliance, and adherence to organizational policies and procedures.
* Enter manual and hardcopy order requests into the Lawson ERP system to generate purchase orders.
* Ensure all purchase orders are confirmed, including pricing, unit of measure (UOM), and product availability. Follow up with Transaction Management or suppliers if confirmations are not received by the beginning of the next business day.
* Review non-file purchase requisition items to determine whether an existing ERP system item should be utilized.
* Process electronic requisitions and inventory control recommended reorder requests to generate purchase orders.
* Redirect orders to contracted suppliers when product conversions have been approved by Regional Resource Groups, the local Product Conversion Committee, and department stakeholders to support compliance goals.
* Support the product return process by obtaining and maintaining appropriate vendor documentation.

**Issue Resolution**

* Route orders appropriately for medical supplies, expedite open orders, facilitate product substitutions for backordered items, and verify pricing against contractual agreements.
* Investigate and resolve pricing discrepancies, backorder issues, and supplier-related concerns in collaboration with customers and vendors.
* Resolve product quality issues by troubleshooting concerns identified by departments and coordinating corrective actions with suppliers.
* Coordinate acceptance testing with suppliers and hospital departments, report results, and follow up on outstanding issues until equipment is functioning according to specifications.
* Review, approve, or route invoice discrepancies when invoices cannot be matched to purchase orders.
* Partner with Finance to ensure accurate pricing, proper system maintenance, and adherence to negotiated contract pricing.

**Vendor Relations**

* Communicate with vendors regarding the procurement of supplies, equipment, and service contracts to ensure accuracy of products, pricing, and delivery terms.
* Coordinate with suppliers to understand and manage site preparation requirements for equipment installations.
* Schedule equipment deliveries in accordance with electrical, biomedical, and other facility requirements.
* Facilitate equipment repair requests and coordinate loaner equipment when needed to ensure continuity of operations.

**Process Improvement**

* Collaborate with internal departments to identify opportunities for process improvements, product standardization, and enhanced item cross-referencing.
* Support initiatives that improve purchasing efficiency, contract compliance, and data accuracy.

**Emergency Procurement**

* Process urgent and overnight purchase requests to support patient care and operational needs.
* Respond promptly to end-user requests and provide confirmation of emergency orders.
* Coordinate same-day pickup or delivery of critical products from local suppliers to ensure uninterrupted operations.

The organization has already established foundational procurement processes, governance frameworks, systems, and transformation initiatives. The successful candidate will inherit a capable procurement team and an established transformation roadmap, building upon these foundations to further mature, optimize, and scale procurement capabilities across the enterprise while preserving business agility and enabling continued growth.

**Job Description**
IREN is building the infrastructure behind the next era of AI. We design, build, and operate massive-scale data centers, and we're racing to deploy some of the largest fleets of GPU and CPU compute on the planet. This isn't incremental growth — it's a full-throttle sprint to power the frontier of AI and high-performance computing. Our Network Sourcing team sits at the center of that mission, securing the switches, optics, fiber, and backbone infrastructure that let IREN's data centers come online and stay connected as fast as anyone in the industry. 
  
  
The Role 
  
IREN is looking for a Technical Sourcing Manager, Fiber & Backbone Infrastructure to take full ownership of the physical fiber network IREN builds and owns end-to-end — from intra-data-center and hall-to-hall fiber through the long-haul backbone routes connecting IREN's sites. This is not a support role — you'll own the manufacturers, connector and passive suppliers, and outside-plant construction and permitting relationships that keep fiber ahead of, not behind, IREN's build schedule. If you love solving problems where construction, permitting, and materials sourcing all collide, and want to see your work show up as a hall lighting up on schedule or a new route connecting two sites — this is the seat for you. You'll operate with real autonomy, direct visibility to the Director, Network Sourcing, and the mandate to shape how IREN sources and builds owned fiber infrastructure at scale. 
  
  
**Job Requirements**

* Own fiber and backbone infrastructure sourcing end-to-end: commercial negotiations, pricing, contracting, and vendor/contractor governance.

* Stay ahead of a supply-constrained fiber and connector market: track cable and high-density MPO/MTP/MMC availability and get out in front of shortages before they become blockers.
* Partner directly with Facilities, Construction, Network Engineering, and Legal to keep fiber and backbone timelines locked in step with build, permitting, and go-live milestones.
* Lead RFQ/RFP processes and cost modeling for fiber materials, splicing labor, and OSP construction contracts, including unit-based (per-mile/per-foot) pricing structures.
* Negotiate supply agreements, unit-price construction contracts, and quality/testing standards (OTDR, insertion loss, return loss) that protect IREN's speed and build quality.
* Own supplier and contractor performance — delivery, quality, escalations, and business reviews — and hold partners to a standard worthy of IREN's growth.
* Build and maintain rolling 12–24 month demand forecasts for fiber materials, labor, and route construction with facilities and network engineering.
* Hunt for cost-savings and risk-mitigation opportunities: route diversity, dual-sourcing of materials, and construction contract restructuring — anything that gives IREN an edge.

**Job Responsibilities**

* 7+ years of experience in sourcing or procurement spanning fiber optic cable, structured cabling, and outside-plant/long-haul telecommunications infrastructure; data center, hyperscale, or telecom carrier experience strongly preferred.

* Demonstrated success negotiating complex commercial and construction agreements, including unit-based (per-mile/per-foot) contract structures.
* Working knowledge of permitting, easements, and right-of-way processes (municipal, utility, and railroad crossings) and their impact on construction timelines.
* Battle-tested experience navigating supply-constrained materials markets and long-lead-time construction/permitting cycles.
* Sharp analytical instincts — comfortable sizing fiber counts and route capacity against multi-site buildout roadmaps.
* Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills; equally at home with facilities, construction, network engineering, and legal.
* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, Business, or related field (or equivalent experience).

Preferred 
  

* Existing relationships with fiber and cable manufacturers (e.g., Corning, OFS, Fujikura, Prysmian, Sumitomo) and OSP construction contractors.
* Experience planning route diversity and redundancy for owned backbone networks.
* Deep familiarity with data center commissioning timelines and how fiber delivery integrates with facility construction and rack integration schedules.

You will be responsible for identifying cost-saving opportunities, leading sourcing and contract negotiations, optimizing procurement processes, and ensuring the timely acquisition of goods and services that support business operations. This role offers the opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams, influence business decisions, and contribute to continuous improvement in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Procurement Strategy & Governance**

* Deploy and own the Linehaul procurement strategy aligned with network design, volume forecasts, and service requirements.
* Establish procurement governance, rate discipline, and contract standardization across the linehaul network.
* Drive annual savings, cost avoidance, and productivity improvements.

**Strategic Sourcing & Contracting**

* Lead large-scale RFPs, tenders, and auctions using digital sourcing tools (e.g., Keelvar).
* Negotiate commercial frameworks with core and regional linehaul providers.
* Ensure the majority of linehaul spend is covered by robust, compliant contracts.

**Supplier & Capacity Management**

* Develop strategic partnerships with key linehaul carriers.
* Ensure capacity readiness for peak seasons and network changes.
* Monitor supplier performance, financial health, and service reliability.

**Network Optimization & Execution**

* Partner with Network, Operations, and Product teams to support route optimization, linehaul balancing, and asset utilization.
* Support new lanes, hubs, and structural network changes from a procurement standpoint.

**Digital Enablement & Analytics**

* Drive adoption of advanced sourcing and optimization tools (e.g., Keelvar).
* Improve spend transparency, award logic, and data-driven decision-making.
* Leverage analytics to support sourcing strategies and carrier mix decisions.

**Stakeholder Leadership**

* Act as a senior procurement partner to Operations, Network, Commercial, and Finance leadership.
* Support customer solutions and pricing strategies with linehaul cost intelligence.

**Key Stakeholders**
**Internal:**
Operations, Network Design, Product, Finance, Legal, Commercial, Program Management,
**Maersk Brokerage**
**External:**
Linehaul carriers, strategic transportation partners, sourcing technology providers
  
  
**Key KPIs**

* Annual linehaul savings and cost avoidance
* % of linehaul spend under contract
* Capacity coverage vs. forecasted demand
* Tender and auction utilization rate (Keelvar)
* Carrier performance vs. SLAs
* Network cost per mile / per shipment

**Required Qualifications**

* 5+ years of experience in procurement, preferably within transportation procurement and/or transportation operations.
* Strong financial acumen and analytical capabilities.
* Advanced proficiency with Excel and experience creating presentations and reporting in PowerPoint.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
* Professional, approachable, and task-oriented personality.
* Ability to serve as a liaison with terminal managers and business stakeholders.
* Willingness to travel regionally as needed.

**Salary**
: $80,000 - $90,000\\*
  
  
**Benefits:**
Full time employees are eligible for Health Insurance, Paid Time Off, and 401k Match

**About Radiant**
Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based startup building the world’s first mass-produced, portable nuclear microreactors. The company’s first reactor, Kaleidos, is a 1-megawatt, fail-safe microreactor that can be transported anywhere power is needed and run for up to 5 years without refueling. Portable nuclear power with rapid-deploy capability can replace similar-sized diesel generators and provide critical asset support for hospitals, data centers, remote sites, and military bases. Radiant’s unique, practical approach to nuclear development leverages modern software engineering to rapidly deliver safe, factory-built microreactors that use existing, well-qualified materials. Founded in 2020, Radiant is on track to test its first reactor at the Idaho National Laboratory this summer, with initial customer deliveries beginning in 2028.
  
  
**About The Role**
Radiant is seeking a proactive and technically-minded
**Strategic Sourcing Manager**
to lead the discovery, qualification, and development of new suppliers and manufacturing technologies in support of our micro-reactor program. This role is foundational to expanding Radiant's supply base into new commodities, processes, and capabilities as our designs mature. Unlike a traditional buyer role, this position is heavily front-end weighted — finding the right suppliers before a part exists in production, matching engineering intent to real-world manufacturing capability, and shepherding new suppliers and parts from concept through qualification and into reliable, on-time delivery. You will work closely with Engineering, Supplier Development Engineers (SDEs), Quality Assurance, and Operations to build Radiant's supplier ecosystem from the ground up.
  
  
**Responsibilities & Duties**

* Supplier Discovery: Proactively identify and research new potential suppliers and manufacturing technologies across domestic and (where permissible) international markets, including specialized, niche, or emerging process capabilities relevant to nuclear-grade hardware.
* Design-to-Supplier Matching: Partner with Engineering to interpret drawings, specifications, and material requirements, and translate them into supplier search criteria — matching part complexity, tolerances, materials, and process needs to real supplier capability.
* Supplier Vetting & Qualification: Lead initial supplier vetting, including capability assessments, facility questionnaires, and preliminary risk screening, in coordination with SDEs and Quality on technical and quality qualification.
* Onboarding: Own the end-to-end onboarding process for new suppliers — from first contact through NDA, capability review, and entry into Radiant's approved supplier base.
* R&D & New Technology Sourcing: Research and evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and processes (e.g., additive manufacturing, novel joining/forming methods) that could unlock new sourcing pathways or de-risk critical components.
* New Part Introduction (NPI) Support: Act as the commercial and program-management thread for new parts through their qualification lifecycle — coordinating purchase order issuance, first articles, prototype builds, and pilot runs between the supplier, Engineering, and Quality.

**PURCHASING AND RECIEVING MANAGER**
**DEPARTMENT:**
A&G
  
  
**REPORTS TO:**
Director of Finance
  
  
**Position Summary**
The Purchasing and Receiving Manager ensures seamless procurement and delivery of goods and supplies for all Coury Hospitality properties. This role supports the operational and financial efficiency of the organization by accurately managing purchase orders, receiving deliveries, maintaining inventory records, and collaborating with vendors and internal teams to guarantee quality, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness.
  
  
**Primary Job Duties**

* Process purchase orders in accordance with property needs, budget, and Coury Hospitality procurement policies.
* Identify and establish relationships with vendors, negotiate prices and delivery terms while ensuring quality standards.
* Track order status and proactively resolve issues such as backorders, delays, or discrepancies.
* Maintain accurate purchasing records and assist with audits and inventory reconciliation.
* Receive incoming deliveries, verifying quantities, quality, and specifications against purchase orders.
* Inspect items for damage, expiration dates, and compliance with Coury Hospitality standards.
* Ensure proper storage of inventory according to safety and operational guidelines.
* Maintain accurate receiving logs and update inventory management systems in real-time.
* Communicate effectively with department heads to anticipate inventory needs.
* Coordinate with Finance for invoice approvals and timely vendor payments.
* Report any discrepancies, shortages, or quality issues to management promptly.
* Adhere to Coury Hospitality’s standards for cleanliness, safety, and efficiency in receiving and storage areas.
* Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to streamline procurement and inventory processes.
* Support team members and contribute to a positive, guest-focused work environment.

Additional tasks and responsibilities may be assigned at the discretion of the manager. Furthermore, tasks and responsibilities may be added or revised based on the volume of business and the need for the work to be completed at the present time.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills And Abilities**

* High school diploma or equivalent; associate degree preferred.
* 1–3 years of experience in purchasing, receiving, or inventory management, preferably in hospitality, food service, or retail.
* Knowledge of procurement processes, vendor relations, and inventory systems.
* Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to multitask.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and inventory management software.
* Ability to lift and move inventory as needed (typically 30–50 lbs).
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

**Physical Demands**

* Prolonged sitting at a desk while working on a computer (frequent to constant).
* Frequent use of hands and fingers for typing, data entry, and operating office equipment.
* Occasional standing and walking within the office to access files, printers, or meet with employees.

The Sourcing Manager will lead the development, and commercialization of white label products that expand and strengthen the Ruggable assortment. This role will partner closely with Creative, Design, Merchandising, and Operations to identify assortment opportunities and translate them into compelling, brand-right product offerings. This role will leverage the capabilities, constructions, and product offerings of global suppliers, identifying products that can be customized, and adapted through a Ruggable lens. The ideal candidate combines a strong product eye with deep sourcing and product development experience, understands how to evaluate supplier capabilities and commercially viable products, and can move quickly from assortment opportunity to market-ready product.
  
  
**What You’ll Do:**

* Lead white label sourcing, product development and commercialization from initial assortment opportunity through production and launch.
* Partner closely with Merchandising and Creative teams to identify gaps and opportunities within the existing assortment and translate those needs into actionable product and sourcing strategies.
* Research global markets, suppliers, manufacturing regions, trade shows, and emerging product categories to identify new products, materials, constructions, and vendor capabilities.
* Identify and onboard new suppliers capable of filling specific assortment needs while meeting Ruggable standards.
* Evaluate existing supplier product lines and capabilities to identify products that can be customized, or adapted to align with Ruggable’s design sensibility and customer expectations.
* Develop clear product briefs for suppliers that communicate aesthetic direction, target costs, quality expectations, performance requirements, and key commercial objectives.

* Proactively identify and resolve development, costing, quality, capacity, and manufacturing issues that could impact product launches.
* Conduct supplier and factory visits to evaluate capabilities, review product opportunities, manage development, and strengthen vendor partnerships.
* Maintain awareness of competitive assortments, consumer trends, emerging materials, manufacturing capabilities, and relevant developments within the home furnishings and textile markets.
* Drive continuous improvement within the white label development process, including supplier onboarding, product evaluation, sampling, costing, documentation, and cross-functional workflows.

* Bachelor’s degree in Product Development, Textiles, Merchandising, Sourcing, Business, or a related field; equivalent relevant industry experience may be considered.
* 7+ years of progressive product development, sourcing, or related experience, preferably within rugs, home textiles, home furnishings, or adjacent consumer product categories.
* Extensive experience working directly with overseas suppliers and factories.
* Demonstrated ability to identify and evaluate new vendors, manufacturing capabilities, and commercially viable product opportunities.
* Strong understanding of the product development and commercialization process from initial concept or product

Symbotic is seeking a highly motivated NPI Procurement Manager to join our Procurement organization within the Strategic Launch Team. ITW Shakeproof serves major automotive and industrial OEMs and their tier suppliers with metal, cold-headed fasteners totaling approximately $210M in revenue. ****Job Description:****
ITW Shakeproof is seeking a
**Tool Room Buyer**
who is responsible for direct oversight and management of the Machesney Park Plant Tool Room. The Tooling Buyer is responsible for sourcing, purchasing, expediting, and managing tooling and related supplies required to support fastener manufacturing operations. This position works closely with Engineering, Tool Room, Production, Quality, Maintenance, and outside suppliers to ensure the timely availability of tooling that meets required specifications, quality standards, cost objectives, and production schedules.
  
  
The Tool Buyer will have particular responsibility for tooling used in cold heading, forming, threading, secondary operations, and inspection processes. ****Essential Responsibilities:****
**Tooling Procurement**

* Purchase production tooling including dies, punches, pins, inserts, knockouts, cutters, thread rolls, taps, drills, carbide tooling, gauges, and other manufacturing tooling.
* Review purchase requisitions, engineering drawings, specifications, tooling requirements, and historical purchasing information before placing orders.
* Obtain and evaluate supplier quotations based on price, quality, lead time, capability, and total cost.
* Create and maintain purchase orders and ensure accurate pricing, quantities, revisions, delivery dates, and specifications.
* Monitor open tooling orders and proactively expedite critical items to prevent production interruptions.
* Coordinate emergency tooling requirements when breakdowns, excessive wear, quality issues, or unexpected demand threaten production schedules.
* Identify cost-saving opportunities through competitive bidding, alternative sourcing, blanket orders, volume agreements, standardization, and supplier negotiations.

* Develop and maintain effective relationships with tooling manufacturers, machine shops, carbide suppliers, gauge suppliers, and other key vendors.
* Evaluate supplier performance related to quality, delivery, responsiveness, lead time, and cost.
* Work with suppliers to resolve late deliveries, incorrect tooling, quality concerns, invoice discrepancies, and other performance issues.
* Identify and qualify alternate suppliers to reduce single-source risk and improve supply continuity.
* Support supplier negotiations and sourcing strategies for high-use and critical tooling.
* Coordinate tooling repair, rework, sharpening, recoating, and refurbishment when economically appropriate.

**Manufacturing & Technical Support**

* Work closely with Tool Room, Engineering, Production, Quality, and Maintenance personnel to understand tooling requirements and priorities.
* Read and interpret tooling drawings, prints, specifications, part numbers, revisions, and basic dimensional requirements.
* Develop an understanding of tooling used in cold heading, cold forming, thread rolling, machining, trimming, pointing, and secondary operations.
* Ensure suppliers receive current drawings and revision information when sourcing custom tooling.
* Assist Engineering and Manufacturing in sourcing tooling for new-product launches, process changes, and continuous-improvement projects.
* Support resolution of tooling-related production issues through communication with internal stakeholders and suppliers.
* Maintain awareness of tooling lead times and communicate potential shortages or production risks to appropriate personnel.

**Inventory & Cost Control**

* Help establish appropriate inventory levels for frequently used, long-lead-time, and production-critical tooling.
* Review tooling usage and purchasing history to identify opportunities to improve stocking strategies.
* Monitor excessive tooling usage, unusual purchasing patterns, and significant cost changes.
* Assist in developing min/max, reorder point, safety stock, and/or Kanban systems for commonly used tooling.

The successful candidate should possess:
  
  

* Strong purchasing and negotiation skills.
* Ability to read and understand basic engineering drawings

The Buyer is responsible for procuring quality goods and services that meet LATICRETE’s cost, quality, and delivery objectives, while maintaining appropriate inventory levels and ensuring compliance with company policies. The Buyer collaborates with Planning, Operations, Finance, and Supplier partners to execute procurement plans driven by demand signals and MRP, and to proactively escalate issues that could impact supply.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
*Additional duties and responsibilities may be assigned as necessary.*
**Inventory Management (35%):**

* Implement stocking models considering factors such as demand forecasts, lead times, logistics, and supplier capabilities.
* Conduct regular reviews and adjustments to stocking models based on changing demand patterns to maintain optimal inventory levels.
* Support inventory risk identification (e.g., potential stockouts, long lead time exposure) and communicate mitigation options to Planning and Procurement leadership.
* Review and maintain purchasing master data (e.g., lead times, order multiples, safety stock) and planning parameters to reflect current supply and supplier capabilities.

**Procurement (30%):**

* Execute MRP action messages and translate approved demand signals into timely purchase actions to maintain targeted inventory and service levels.
* Create and manage purchase orders in line with cost, quality, and delivery targets; track orders and coordinate inbound logistics to meet need dates.
* Confirm acknowledgments and update stakeholders on order status and changes.
* Resolve day-to-day supplier issues (price, delivery, invoice discrepancies), escalating to management as needed.

**Supplier Relationship Management (10%):**

* Cultivate and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with suppliers to ensure reliability, quality, and timeliness of deliveries.
* Capture delivery/quality issues and escalate to suppliers and internal management as appropriate.
* Support data collection for supplier performance tracking (OTIF, responsiveness), coordinating with Procurement leadership for periodic reviews.
* Champion ethical sourcing practices and sustainability initiatives within the supply chain, working closely with suppliers to promote responsible sourcing and environmental stewardship.

**Collaboration (25%):**

* Partner with Demand Planning on forecast signals
* Coordinate with Operations, Warehousing/Logistics, and Finance to align purchasing activity with production schedules and cash flow considerations.
* Contribute to clear, timely status updates to enable cross-functional decision making

The Senior Supply Chain Planner and Buyer is a senior level individual contributor responsible for maintaining material availability while balancing customer service, quality, inventory investment, cost, and supply risk. The position translates demand into actionable supply plans, executes purchasing activities, manages inventory performance, and develops productive supplier relationships.
  
  
This role works closely with Sales, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Warehouse, and other supply chain partners to identify constraints, resolve shortages, and improve the accuracy and reliability of planning and procurement processes. This is a role for someone who wants to use their analytical and interactive skills in order to have a direct impact on an organization’s supply chain.
  
  
**Essential Functions**
**Purchasing**

* Manage the end-to-end purchasing cycle for assigned commodities, components, and suppliers, including requisition review, purchase order placement, order confirmation, receipt follow-up, and issue resolution.
* Convert material requirements and approved requests into purchase orders using ERP information, production priorities, supplier lead times, order quantities, pricing, and inventory targets.
* Monitor open purchase orders and supplier commitments. Expedite, defer, reschedule, or cancel orders as business needs change, and communicate material risks to affected teams.
* Request and evaluate supplier quotations, compare total cost and commercial terms, negotiate within delegated authority, and recommend sourcing decisions to the Director of Procurement.
* Maintain accurate purchasing data, including pricing, lead times, order quantities, supplier information, acknowledgments, and purchase order records. Resolve receiving, invoice, and quantity discrepancies with internal teams and suppliers.

**Inventory Management**

* Identify inventory control issues and monitor compliance, ensure that warehouse activities are in full compliance with federal, regulatory safety, labor, worker’s compensation, and health/safety requirements.
* Establish and maintain planning parameters such as safety stock, reorder points, minimum and maximum levels, lead times, and order quantities for assigned materials.
* Analyze inventory levels and usage to reduce stockouts, excess inventory, obsolete material, and avoidable carrying cost while supporting production and customer requirements.
* Track and report inventory performance using measures such as service level, inventory turns, days of supply, excess and obsolete inventory, and material availability.
* Support cycle counts and physical inventories, investigate variances, identify root causes, and coordinate corrective actions with Warehouse, Operations, Finance, and Quality.

**Planning and Forecasting**

* Develop and maintain demand forecasts using sales history, open orders, customer and market information, product plans, promotions, and input from Sales and Marketing.

**Summary - Job Responsibilities - Activities:**

The Junior Buyer supports day-to-day procurement activities to ensure materials, components, supplies, and services are available when needed at the right cost, quality, and delivery terms. Working under the guidance of senior purchasing staff, this role prepares and maintains purchase orders, communicates with suppliers, monitors delivery performance, resolves routine supply issues, and keeps purchasing data accurate. The Junior Buyer collaborates with Planning, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and other internal teams to support production and business requirements.

**Functions:**

• Create, issue, and maintain purchase orders in accordance with approved requisitions, specifications, pricing, and company procedures.

• Review purchase order acknowledgments and follow up with suppliers to confirm pricing, quantities, and delivery dates.

• Monitor open orders and expedite, reschedule, or communicate changes to support production and operational priorities.

• Request and evaluate supplier quotations, prepare basic bid comparisons, and support sourcing and negotiation activities.

• Maintain accurate supplier, item, lead-time, pricing, and delivery information in the ERP or purchasing system.

• Coordinate with suppliers and internal teams to resolve routine shortages, late deliveries, invoice discrepancies, quality concerns, and documentation issues.

• Track supplier performance and assist with supplier reviews, corrective actions, and continuous-improvement initiatives.

• Support inventory objectives by reviewing demand, order quantities, lead times, and excess or obsolete material risks.

• Identify cost-saving, risk-reduction, and process-improvement opportunities and escalate recommendations to senior purchasing staff.

• Maintain organized purchasing records and follow applicable quality, regulatory, contractual, and company requirements.

• Perform additional procurement and supply-chain duties as assigned.

• Associate degree in business, supply chain, operations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, business administration, engineering, or a related discipline preferred.

• Up to two years of experience in purchasing, materials, planning, inventory, customer service, or a related business function; internships and cooperative education experience are welcome.

• Experience in a manufacturing, distribution, or regulated environment preferred.

• Exposure to ERP or MRP systems and purchasing fundamentals preferred.

• Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through, and ability to manage multiple priorities.

Angayut, LLC is seeking a Senior Procurement Analyst to lead policy-support activities for the PBGC Procurement Department. This key-personnel position will research federal acquisition requirements and leading practices; draft policy, procedures, templates, audit responses, and training materials; provide procurement data analytics; and support PBGC acquisition systems and users.

  

The Senior Procurement Analyst will provide advice, recommendations, analysis, and draft products for Government review and approval. The position requires strong command of the FAR and federal procurement policy, excellent research and writing skills, and the ability to translate legislative, regulatory, OMB, Executive Order, audit, and system changes into practical guidance and tools.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

  

  
* Lead Task 5 acquisition and procurement policy management, policy research, training coordination, data analytics, and systems-support activities.
  
* Research legislative changes, FAR and agency policy issuances, OMB memoranda, Executive Orders, audit findings, leading practices, and system capabilities affecting PBGC procurement operations.
  
* Draft recommendations, new policies, policy revisions, official reports, assessments, audit responses, standard operating procedures, and end-user guidance for Government review and approval.
  
* Develop and update standard acquisition templates, including requirement documents, solicitation documents, award memoranda, BPA templates, and Technical Evaluation Panel reports for LPTA and tradeoff acquisitions.
  
* Analyze procurement data from PRISM, SharePoint, FPDS, SAM.gov, and other authorized sources to support policy decisions, program management, reporting, and process improvement.
  
* Develop data-gathering methods, analytical techniques, performance measures, reports, dashboards, and assessments supporting procurement policy programs.
  
* Prepare training presentations, reports, training-request documentation, and acquisition-policy research supporting PBGC training activities.
  
* Coordinate Section 508-compliant policy, training, template, and end-user products.
  
* Support PRISM and related procurement systems through data entry, database maintenance, error correction, access-request routing, customer and vendor communications, issue documentation, testing, and follow-up.
  
* Assist with Data Act reporting, procurement-system change analysis, upgrades, testing, outages, and coordination with PBGC IT subject-matter experts.
  
* Maintain non-inherently governmental boundaries; PBGC officials retain responsibility for determining and approving agency policy.

* **Education:**
  Bachelor's degree in acquisition management, business, public policy, public administration, finance, law, information systems, or a related field preferred; an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience may be considered.
  
* **Experience:**

* Advanced knowledge of the FAR and federal procurement principles, policies, procedures, and contract-writing practices.
  
* Demonstrated experience drafting or revising acquisition policy, SOPs, standard templates, audit or OMB responses, training materials, or executive-level reports.
  
* Experience conducting procurement data analysis using contract-writing systems, FPDS, SAM.gov, SharePoint, spreadsheets, databases, and other federal data sources.
  
* Experience with PRISM or a comparable federal contract-writing system, including data quality, user support, testing, reporting, or process-change coordination, preferred.
  
* FAC-C, DAWIA Contracting, NCMA certification, acquisition-policy credential, or comparable formal acquisition training preferred.

* Lead cross-functional initiatives and provide guidance to project teams to support operational improvement and network optimization.
